statement_record.book: Gr is the free category on the graph with two vertices Arrow, Vertex and two parallel arrows source, target : Arrow → Vertex, no equations. A Gr-instance I : Gr → Set is EXACTLY a graph (I(Vertex) the vertices, I(Arrow) the arrows, I(source)/I(target) the endpoint maps); every graph arises this way. Hence the objects of Gr-Inst = Set^Gr are graphs and its morphisms — natural transformations with components α_Vertex, α_Arrow — are exactly graph homomorphisms, the naturality squares at source and target being preservation of endpoints.
statement_record.intree: The schema exists as Parallel (two objects, two parallel non-identity arrows), so Gr = Parallel^op; one graph is exhibited as an instance by Presheaf_Graph : Parallel^op ⟶ Sets with fobj ParX := nat (vertices), fobj ParY := nat*nat (edges), fmap of the two arrows := fst (source) and snd (target); Gr-Inst is available as [Parallel^op, Sets] from Fun; and the category of graphs in the direct presentation is QuiverCategory over Class Quiver / Class QuiverHomomorphism.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the two halves exist but the IDENTIFICATION between them — the whole content of the construction — is never stated. In-tree there is (a) the schema and one hand-built instance, and (b) an independently defined category of graphs, with no functor, isomorphism or equivalence connecting [Parallel^op, Sets] to QuiverCategory. Program Definition FreeOnQuiver : Category := {| obj := @nodes G; hom := tlist edges; homset := fun i j => {| equiv := tlist_quiver_equiv _ _ _ |}; id := fun _ => tnil; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => g +++ f |} — morphisms are paths of generating edges, i.e. the free category on a graph with no equations.
